## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Fresh project. Need to build a complete playable 2D JRPG for phone/tablet. Requirements: turn-based JRPG, character creation, job classes, skill trees, open world mechanics, choices-matter storylines with continuation arcs depending on choices.

No framework. Build with vanilla HTML/CSS/JS + canvas. Need to serve. Let's check runtime dir & playwright availability.

Let's plan a robust, high-quality game. Scope must be big but achievable. Let's design:

Single-page canvas game, landscape recommended but works portrait. Touch controls, virtual joystick/dpad, action button. Save to localStorage.

Tiles / world map open world with multiple regions and towns, NPCs, quests, random encounters, world map with several areas connected openly (walk freely between zones via exits). Turn-based battles with party of up to 4? Character creation: choose name, appearance (color), class among 6 (Warden/Knight, Mage, Rogue/Shadowblade, Cleric, Ranger, Arcanist?) plus stat bonus and origin which affects story. Job classes & skill trees: each class gets skill tree unlocking with skill points on level up. Choices matter: major choices in story branches, flags stored, continuation arcs: two-act structure with distinct endings/arcs.

Let me design a polished game:

Title: "Aetherfall: Emberwake" or "The Hollow Crown". Let's go with **Emberfall** — 2D pixel-ish JRPG.

Core loop:
1. Title screen → New Game / Continue
2. Character creation: name, class (4 classes), appearance colors, origin background (3 options) - each affects story choice and starting stats.
3. Overworld: tilemap-based 2D exploration with smooth camera, open world regions: Emberfield (starting village), Greenwood, Ashen Marsh, Cinder Peaks, Hollow Citadel. Connections on edges; open traversal; NPCs with dialog; interactables (chests, save crystals, quest markers).
4. Random-ish encounters while walking in grass / zone encounter meters.
5. Battle: turn-based ATB? Pure turn-based with speed order shown. Party: player + recruitable companions depending on choices. Actions: Attack, Skill (tree skills, MP), Item, Guard, Flee. Enemy AI. Status effects (burn, poison, chill, stun...). Animations, damage numbers, screen shake.
6. Progression: XP, level up, skill points, skill tree UI per character. Jobs: each character class with tree nodes. Maybe job switching? "job classes" - allow player class + companion classes.
7. Story: choice moments with branching arcs, flags. 2 acts, multiple endings. Continuation arcs: if you spare the boss → "Redemption arc" act 2 differences; if you join the Ashen Order → "Shadow arc". Implement at least 3 distinct endings and arc-specific scenes.
8. Save/load localStorage with autosave.

UI: Canvas for world & battle, DOM for menus? Mixing is fine. Use canvas full-screen with DOM overlays for dialog and menus for crisp text and touch friendliness. Actually easier: canvas game + HTML UI overlays styled with CSS. Touch controls via buttons.

Mobile: responsive, on-screen D-pad + action buttons, tap NPC to interact, dialog large.

Screenshots: Need playwright-cli. Check.

Let's design the game deeply.

Game name: **EMBERWAKE — The Ashen Crown**

Features checklist:
- Character creation: name, 6 classes, origin (3), appearance (4 palettes), stat allocation maybe 3 bonus points. Keep simple but meaningful.
- Job classes: 6 jobs with distinct skills, stats, skill trees of ~9 nodes each (passives + active skills).
- Skill trees UI with tiers/node connections, SP earned per level.
- Open world: a tile world of 5 connected regions with no loading? Open-world mechanics: free roam, multiple towns, day/night? Weather? Let's implement:
  - Large seamless overworld composed of regions on a big map (e.g., 120x90 tiles) with biome tiles and placed structures. Camera follows, torch lighting at night maybe. An open world with free traversal, discoverable chests, NPCs, fast-travel waypoints, side quests, bounty board, "world events" (shrines), encounter zones.
  - Mobile touch: virtual joystick (drag anywhere left half), action button + menu. Auto interact prompt.
  - Minimap and quest compass.
- Choices matter: dialogue choices with flags; Acts; ending variants; companion recruitment/permadeath? Keep companion loyalty.
- Turn-based battle: party up to 3 (player + 2 companions), enemy groups, initiative order by SPD, skills with elements/status, guard, items, flee, auto-battle? Battle UI with sprites drawn in canvas (vector shapes) — need decent art. We can draw stylized characters with canvas shapes, not pixel sprites. Could generate pixel art sprites procedurally? Simpler: draw layered silhouettes with shapes and shadows, animations (bob, lunge, hit flash). Add particle effects.

Art direction: moody dark fantasy with ember orange/teal palette. Canvas rendering: tiles with procedural texture noise (deterministic), trees/rocks/houses drawn with shapes, ambient particles (fireflies/embers), vignette. Title screen with animated embers and logo.

Party portraits: draw via canvas or CSS gradients with rune sigils. Could generate SVG portraits procedurally based on class/color. I'll create simple canvas portraits.

Audio: WebAudio procedural SFX + music? Adding simple generative music loop would elevate. Implement WebAudio small synth with toggle. Maybe simple loop for explore/battle/title. Keep modest but present.

Story structure:
- Prologue: village of Hearthfall, Emberwake festival, the sky cracks (the Sundering), Ashen Order attacks, you awaken power.
- Act I: Seek the three Emberkeys across three regions (Greenwood, Marsh, Peaks), with choices:
  - Choice 1: Save the elder vs pursue the raider (affects companion/items).
  - Choice 2 at Greenwood: side with Warden Elowen (order/control) or the Freewood (freedom); gives arc flags.
  - Choice 3 at Marsh: spare or kill the Witch of Mire; if spare, she joins later / redemption arc.
  - Choice 4 at Peaks: give Emberkey to the Ashen Order envoy (join them → Shadow arc) or resist.
- Act II: Citadel; depending on flags, allies differ, final confrontation with the Ashen King / Vaelor. Endings:
  - "Dawnforge" (unite factions, high trust)
  - "Ashen Crown" (take the crown, dominate)
  - "Redemption" (spare Vaelor, restore the cycle)
  - "Hollow" (bad ending if low trust / let the flame die)
- Continue arcs: after ending, New Game+ with "continuation" epilogue choices? Requirement "choices matter storylines with continuation arcs depending on choices" — implement branching Act II and distinct epilogue arcs, plus post-game "Chronicle" screen showing consequences and unlocked arc. Also allow continuing after final battle into post-game open world with epilogue quests depending on choice. That's a lot. Let's implement a solid branching act 2 and epilogue text plus New Game+ carrying a "legacy" perk.

Scope needs to be finishable. I'll write maybe 4000+ lines across files. Need to be systematic.

Files:
- index.html — shell, screens, HUD, overlays, touch controls.
- css/style.css — responsive, layout.
- js/data.js — classes, skills, items, enemies, quests, dialogue, maps? Maybe split:
  - js/data/classes.js
  - js/data/enemies.js
  - js/data/world.js (map generation + NPCs)
  - js/data/story.js (dialogues & choices)
  - js/engine/*.js
Given no build step, use ES modules (works server). Manage imports.

Proposed architecture:
- state.js: game state, save/load, flags, party, inventory, quests.
- audio.js
- ui.js: DOM overlays, dialogue system, menus, toasts, screens.
- world.js: map gen + rendering + movement + interactions + encounters.
- battle.js: battle engine + rendering (canvas battle scene) + UI.
- character.js: creation + skills.
- main.js: boot, game loop, scene switching.

Canvas: one #game canvas, responsive, devicePixelRatio. World and battle drawn on same canvas. Menus in DOM overlay.

Simplify: world rendering on canvas at a fixed internal resolution? Use CSS pixel sizes matching viewport, scale factor. Tile size 48 px world units, camera zoom ~1 for mobile? On phone with 390x844 portrait, showing ~8x17 tiles. Landscape 844x390 shows 17x8. Need responsive. I'll support both orientations, but prompt "rotate for best experience" maybe not needed. UI adapts.

Could design fixed virtual viewport (e.g., 960x540) scaled with letterbox... For mobile portrait that leaves huge bars. Better adaptive camera: canvas full screen, tile = 44 CSS px clamped to viewport. Camera shows variable tiles. Works.

Though UI: world HUD overlays (top-left party status, top-right minimap, bottom touch controls on mobile only? Show touch controls always on coarse pointer, plus keyboard). Provide on-screen D-pad in bottom-left and action/menu buttons bottom-right. Also support drag joystick.

World map: create 5 zones on one big grid with teleport-free transitions? Seamless: Build one 96x72 map, split regions logically, with paths. But generating visually distinct regions manually is work. Alternative: separate zone maps with edge transitions (classic JRPG). "Open world mechanics" can still be zone-based open maps with free exploration. Simpler and manageable: 6 maps each ~40x30, connected via edge exits and world map fast travel. I'd rather do separate maps with custom handcrafted layouts in data arrays.

Handcrafted maps via string arrays at e.g. 40x26 with legend:
- '.' grass, ',' flowers, '#' tree, '~' water, '=' path, '^' mountain, 's' sand, 'b' bridge, 'h' house wall, 'd' door, 'f' fence, 'r' rock, 'g' grave, 'c' crystal, 't' statue, ' ' void?
Use ASCII layouts ~30x20 each; that's substantial but manageable, 6 maps × 20 lines.

Given time, procedural generation with seeded noise plus hand-placed key locations might be more lush. But handcrafted ASCII gives intentional level design and deterministic look. I'll write 6 maps with 36x24 ASCII each.

Zones:
1. hearthfall — Hearthfall Village (start): houses, inn (save/rest), elder's house, forge, festival square, exit south/east to Emberfield. NPCs.
2. emberfield — Emberfield Plains: grass, roads, ruins, chest, shrine, exit to Greenwood (east), Hearthfall (north), Marsh (south).
3. greenwood — Greenwood: ancient forest, Warden camp, village of Mosswood? Boss: Thornwarden. Emberkey of Root. Choice with Elowen.

- Actions: Attack (physical, single), Skills (cost MP), Items, Guard (+DEF, regen MP), Flee (chance). Skills include elemental damage, heal, buffs, debuffs, AoE.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D turn-based JRPG for phone/tablet with character creation, job classes, skill trees, open-world exploration, and choices-matter branching storylines with continuation arcs.
- Work is in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround` (fresh static HTML/JS project, not committed yet).

## Requirements
- 2D game, playable on phone/tablet; responsive touch controls; usable landscape and portrait.
- Turn-based JRPG combat, character creation, job classes, skill trees, open world, choices-matter story with continuation arcs.
- No clarifying questions; note assumptions briefly at finish.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for own checks; viewport ≤1280px; read only latest screenshot.
- Must be a complete, playable build now.
- Static `index.html` at repo root (runtime serves it via `default-start.mjs`; `start.sh` uses `RUNTIME_DIR`).

## Decisions
- Vanilla ES modules + canvas rendering + DOM UI; no build step, no external art/audio assets.
- Title: **Emberwake — The Ashen Crown**.
- 6 classes: `vanguard`, `emberweaver`, `shadowblade`, `warden`, `stormcaller`, `ronin`; each with a 10-node skill tree.
- 3 origins: `hearthbound`, `scholar`, `outcast`; 6 appearance palettes; 3 bonus stat points.
- 6 zones: `hearthfall`, `emberfield`, `greenwood`, `mire`, `peaks`, `citadel`; zone-based open traversal, fast travel, quests, random encounters.
- Party max 4: hero + Kael (`ronin`) + one of Lyra (`emberweaver`) / Seris (`warden`) based on Greenwood choice + optional Sable (`shadowblade`) if witch is spared.
- Story acts: prologue → collect 3 Emberkeys (Thorn/Tide/Cinder) in any order → Citadel final boss Vaelor → branching endings (Dawnforge / Ashen Sovereign / Hollow Dawn etc.), plus NG+ continuation.
- Procedural WebAudio music/SFX; all art drawn procedurally on canvas.
- Save to `localStorage` (`emberwake.chronicle.v1`, autosave key).

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` full app shell with title, character creation, HUD, dialogue, menu, shop, battle UI, cinematic, ending, modal layers.
- `css/style.css` complete dark ember/teal responsive styling including touch joystick, dialogues, menus, battle layout, ending, safe-area support.
- Data: `js/data/classes.js` (classes, skills, trees, origins, palettes, companions), `js/data/items.js`, `js/data/enemies.js`, `js/data/zones.js` (procedural map builders + NPCs/chests/crystals/braziers/sparkles/portals/triggers).
- `js/state.js`: state, stat computation incl. passives/gear/origin/bonus, XP/leveling, skill learning, party/companions, inventory/equipment, quests, save/load, main objective.
- `js/engine/audio.js`: procedural music scenes + many SFX.
- `js/engine/art.js`: helpers, humanoid sprites, enemy sprites (wisp/wolf/husk/plant/toad/wraith/golem/knight/king), portraits, class art.
- `js/engine/world-render.js`: tile ground/objects, trees, houses, crystals, chests, braziers, portals, NPCs, time-of-day lighting, ambient particles, minimap.
- `js/engine/title-render.js`: animated title scene + stylized world map.
- `js/engine/battle-render.js`: battle backgrounds by biome, unit positioning, enemy/ally sprites, enemy HP bars, effects, floaters, shake/flash.
- `js/engine/ui-core.js`: DOM helpers, toast/modal/fade/flash/banner/shake, cinematic runner, dialogue typewriter + choices, HUD/minimap/party rendering, audio hookups.
- `js/engine/ui-create.js`: 3-step character creation (identity/origin, class, appearance/bonus/summary) with preview drawing.
- `js/hooks.js`: central hook registry.
- `js/world.js`: movement/pathfinding, collision, camera, interactions, chests/crystals/braziers/sparkles/signs/altars, portals, triggers, random encounters, story dialogue execution, rendering entry point.
- `js/engine/ui-menu.js`, `ui-shop.js`, `ui-battle.js`, `story.js`, `battle.js`, `main.js` are referenced/imported but **NOT YET CREATED** — current app will fail to load.
- `js/data/zones.js` needs fixes: Greenwood altar is overwritten by `.` after `put(m,19,10,'A')`; boss altar coords mismatch: mire map altar is at `(9,4)` but zone data says `(9,5)`; peaks map main altar at `(22,9)` but data says `(22,4)`; Greenwood has no `boss` entry.
- `js/engine/ui-create.js` passes `extra.bonus`; `state.js` supports `member.bonus` now.
- Duplicate/unused import cleanup needed (`ITEMS` in art.js/title-render, `state` in battle-render, etc.), and `ui-core.js` cinematic title-timeout bug can skip first line if tapped early.
- Uncommitted working tree; no git commit/push yet.

### Active
- Implementing missing `battle.js`, `story.js`, `ui-battle.js`, `ui-menu.js`, `ui-shop.js`, `main.js`, then fixing zone altar data and integration bugs.
- Then run/test with Playwright at `http://localhost:3002`, capture JPEG screenshots, iterate visuals/gameplay.

### Blocked
- App cannot run until `story.js` (exports `STORIES`, `runStory`) and `battle.js` (exports `startBattle`, `battleState`) and `main.js` exist because `world.js` imports them.

## Next Move
1. Create `js/story.js`: export `STORIES` map of generator functions and `runStory(gen, ctx)` step driver. Support yields: `say`, `choice`, `flag`, `give`, `gold`, `join`, `battle`, `shop`, `heal`, `travel`, `toast`, `cinematic`, `modal`, `ending`, `wait`.
2. Create `js/battle.js`: turn-based engine with speed/turn queue, attack/skills/items/guard/flee, targeting, status effects, enemy AI, XP/gold/drops, level-ups, boss phases/enrage, defeat respawn, result object `{victory,fled,defeat,respawn}`; export `battleState`, `startBattle`.
3. Create `js/engine/ui-battle.js`: turn-order strip, party cards, action menu, skill/item lists, target picker, result modal, battle log; wire buttons to engine promises.
4. Create `js/engine/ui-shop.js` and `js/engine/ui-menu.js`: buy/sell/talk shop; menu tabs Status, Skills (tree SVG lines/nodes), Satchel (use/equip/sell), Party, Quests, World map + fast travel, System (save/difficulty/sound/help/title).
5. Implement story content: Hearthfall prologue, 3 Emberkey arcs with choices, side quests (locket, relief, braziers, bounty, moonpetal), Citadel final choice, branching endings + epilogue + NG+.
6. Create `js/main.js`: boot, hooks wiring, scene loop (title/world/battle/ending), resize/DPR, menu open close, title buttons, continue metadata, first-gesture audio init, time/playtime.
7. Fix zone altar coords & Greenwood boss entry; wire cinematics/flags; run validation (node syntax/import checks), serve via `PORT=3002 bash start.sh` (or runtime start), open with `playwright-cli`, fix console errors, capture/review screenshots (desktop + mobile).

## Relevant Files
- `js/world.js`: main exploration loop; imports missing `story.js` and `battle.js`; contains integration assumptions.
- `js/state.js`: central state/progression/save APIs used everywhere.
- `js/data/classes.js`: classes, all `SKILLS`, `TREES`, origins, companions.
- `js/data/zones.js`: maps/NPCs/chests/triggers/portals; needs altar coordinate fixes.
- `js/data/enemies.js`: bestiary incl. bosses `thornwarden`, `mireWitch`, `knightCommander`, `vaelor`, `vaelorUnbound`.
- `js/data/items.js`: consumables/gear/shop stock.
- `js/engine/art.js`: portrait/sprite functions (`drawPortrait`, `drawEnemy`, `drawPerson`, `drawClassArt`).
- `js/engine/battle-render.js`: exported `renderBattle`, `unitPos`, `drawBattleFace`.
- `js/engine/world-render.js`: exported `renderWorld`, `drawMinimap`.
- `js/engine/title-render.js`: exported `renderTitle`, `drawWorldMap`.
- `js/engine/ui-core.js`: dialogue/choice/HUD/modal/cinematic APIs, `advanceDialogue`.
- `js/engine/ui-create.js`: character creation; calls `hooks.newGame`.
- `js/hooks.js`: hook registry to wire in `main.js`.
- `index.html`, `css/style.css`: existing DOM IDs/classes needed by missing UI modules.
- `Agents.md` / `start.sh` / `capture.sh`: runtime conventions and Playwright info (see environment).

## Important Context
- Runtime serves static `index.html`; `start.sh` calls `node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"` with `PORT=3002` for dev. Use `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`, then screenshot.
- `RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime`.
- `world.js` API consumed by UI/story: `world`, `initWorld()`, `enterZone(id,x,y)`, `refreshWorld()`, `updateWorld(dt,W,H)`, `renderWorldScene(ctx,W,H,now)`, `setPaused(v)`, `runDialogue(id,npc)`, `respawnPlayer()`, `campfireRest()`.
- Story runner must call `hooks.travel` for zone transitions; `main.js` must set `hooks.travel = (zone,x,y) => enterZone(...)` (avoid circular imports).
- Battle flow: `startBattle({zone, enemies:[{id,level}], boss, bossName, canFlee})` returns Promise result; `battleState.active` gates main render/update.
- Altar stories expected by `world.js`: Greenwood `grove_heart` (after choosing side), Mire `mire_boss`, Peaks `peaks_boss`, Citadel `final_boss`; triggers: `grove_confrontation`, `grove_heart_hint`, `emberfield_crossroads`, `mire_sable_meet`, `mire_altar_hint`, `peaks_camp_arrival`, `peaks_caldera_hint`, `citadel_hall`; intros: `hearthfall_intro`, `emberfield_intro`, `greenwood_intro`, `mire_intro`, `peaks_intro`, `citadel_intro`.
- Hearthfall flow: Elder Maro (`elder`) must start prologue; prologue battle then `prologueDone`, Kael joins, Act 1 opens. Elder shows `!` until `prologueDone`.
- Side quest state ids: `locket`, `relief`, `braziers`, `bounty`, `moonpetal`; witchnpc shows only if `sparedWitch`; Sable join if spared. Flag names expected in world: `groveChoice`, `groveScene`, `mireBoss`, `sparedWitch`, `prologueDone`, `peaksChoice`, `lastCrystal`, `braziersReward`, `<zone>BossDefeated`.
- `state.keys` computed from emberkey inventory via `countKeys()`; citadel portal locked while `<3`.
- Touch controls: `#joystick/#joy-knob`, `#btn-action`, `#btn-menu`, `#btn-bag`; dialogue advance handled in `ui-core.js`.
- Browser-side imports are ES modules; syntax errors are fatal. Validate with `node --check` per file and a static import smoke test if possible.
- Screenshot workflow: create `screenshots/`, use `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/latest.jpg` after resizing viewport; review only latest image.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

cd "$(dirname "$0")"
/usr/bin/time -p node "${RUNTIME_DIR:?}/scripts/default-start.mjs"

Let's design battle engine.

### battle.js

Exports `battleState` object with:
```
{
 active: false,
 zone: null,
 allies: [],
 enemies: [],
 order: [],
 turnIndex: 0,
 round: 1,
 boss: false,
 bossName: '',
 canFlee: true,
 log: [],

 floaters: [],
 shakeUntil: 0, shakePower: 0, flashUntil: 0, flashColor: '#fff',
 activeUid: null, targetUid: null,
 awaiting: null,   // current pending action promise/resolver
 result: null,
 phase: 'idle' | 'select' | 'anim' | 'end',
 enemyLevels...
}
```

startBattle(opts) returns Promise. It builds units:
- allies from state.party: 
```
{ uid:'a_'+id, side:'ally', member, name, level, hp: member.hp, maxHp, mp, maxMp, stats:statBlock, statuses:[], dead:false, guard:false, reviveUsed:false, fx:{} }
```
- enemies from ENEMIES[id] with level scaling: stats = base + grow*(level-1), hp scaled difficulty.
- `battleState.active=true`, set scene to battle (`hooks.battleStart?` maybe), hide HUD, show battleUI via DOM.
- UI module needs to drive actions. Options: engine calls UI functions imported from ui-battle (direct import) — circular? ui-battle imports battle engine, engine imports ui-battle -> circular ESM but function hoisting should work if used at runtime. Better: engine exposes a callback `battleState.requestAction(unit)` and UI subscribes via `ui-battle.initBattleUI(battleState)`? Or engine has `onUpdate` hooks. Simplest: ui-battle exports `showBattleUI(battleState)` and `chooseAction(unit)` that returns Promise of action; battle.js imports from ui-battle. Circular import: battle.js imports `requestPlayerAction` from ui-battle; ui-battle imports `battleState`/functions from battle.js. In ESM, circular imports work as long as bindings are used after init. Since both modules are loaded by main; battle.js imports ui-battle, ui-battle imports battle. The evaluation order may be tricky: whichever is imported first. If main imports battle then ui-battle, battle evaluates and imports ui-battle which imports battle (partially initialized, battleState export may not yet be initialized if defined with const after imports) — but ui-battle only references battleState inside functions, not top-level, so fine. However `battle.js` uses imported `requestPlayerAction` inside function calls at runtime, and ui-battle binding will be defined by then. Good.

Alternative decouple with hooks. But circular is acceptable. Need caution: ui-battle imports renderBattle? no.

Actions:
- Player action from UI: `{type:'attack'|'skill'|'item'|'guard'|'flee', skillId, itemId, targetUid}`.
- Engine `takeTurn(unit)`:
  - apply start-of-turn status (stun, regen, mpRegen passives)
  - if ally -> requestPlayerAction; if enemy -> ai choose.
  - resolve.
  - check victory/defeat.
  - advance queue.

Turn order: compute initiative each round for alive units: `agi * (1 + status mods) * (0.9 + random*0.2)`, sort desc. Use splice turn. Could maintain `queue` of uids order for round. Simpler each round builds order, UI shows. Turn pointer.

Status effect objects: need runtime representation. Store `{id, turns, ...}` with metadata from STATUSES. Use helpers:
- `addStatus(unit, id, turns, extra)` merging.
- `hasStatus`, `removeStatus`.
- Stat modifiers: effective atk/def/mag/res/agi computed by `unitStat(unit, key)` applying statuses (atkUp .3, weaken -.25, defUp .3, defDown -.3, resUp/down, agiUp/chill) and `guard` (def*1.6?).
- damage calc:
```
phys: base = atk * power - def*0.55 (min 1), variance .9-1.1; crit; element modifiers via weakness/resist.
mag: mag * power - res*0.45
```
Need balance. Level 1 hero vanguard atk 16 vs ashling def 3: 16*1.0 - 3*.55 = 14. Ashling hp 36 → 3 hits. Good. Skill 1.35 → ~20.
Enemy ashling atk 8 vs hero def 17*.55=9.35 → min ~1*? base = 8*1 - 9 = -1 -> min 1. Too weak. Maybe def multiplier 0.35: 8 - 5.95=2. Player def high. Ashling is a caster using mag 11 vs res 9*.45=4 → 7. Fine. Emberwolf atk 12 vs def 17: 12-7.65=4.35. Slow but okay. At level 2-4, enemy atk 14-16 and hero def ~18-20. Damage 6-8 per hit. With 132 hp, fine.

Bosses: thornwarden level? Story sets maybe level 7. base hp 480+62*6=852; atk 26+2.5*6=41; def 18+1.8*6=28.8. Hero level ~6 atk maybe 14+1.7*5=22.5 + gear 5 = 27.5. phys dmg 27.5*1.3 - 28.8*.45=35.8-13=22.8, ~900/23 = 39 hits. Party 3 with skills maybe ~10-15 rounds. OK-ish but could be long. Skills 2x. Fine maybe tune.

}

    input = await handle(op,args,ctx);
    if (input === 'STOP') return 'stopped';

}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D turn-based JRPG for phone/tablet with character creation, job classes, skill trees, open-world exploration, and choices-matter branching storylines with continuation arcs.
- Work is in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround` (fresh static HTML/JS project, uncommitted).

## Requirements
- 2D game, playable on phone/tablet; responsive touch controls; usable in landscape and portrait.
- Turn-based JRPG combat, character creation, job classes, skill trees, open world, choices-matter story with continuation arcs.
- No clarifying questions; note assumptions briefly at finish.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for own checks; viewport ≤1280px; read only latest screenshot.
- Must be a complete, playable build now.
- Static `index.html` at repo root served by runtime.

## Decisions

content.text:
Now need story.js design. But first missing shop and main. The story file is big. Need to create a complete coherent narrative with all expected keys. Let me plan architecture carefully.

### story.js requirements

Exports:
- STORIES: object of generator functions (each takes ctx maybe). world.js calls `runStory(gen, { npc, world })` and story IDs map.
- runStory(gen, ctx): if gen is generator function, create iterator and process yielded commands.
- ENDINGS / buildEndingData.

Story command protocol: yields objects. Use helper functions as generator wrappers? E.g.:

export function* elder({ npc }) { ... yield say(...); const c = yield choice([...]); ...}

But note calling `yield say('...')` returns promise? runStory interpreter handles command shapes. Simpler: commands are objects with `type`, and for commands that need return values (say/choice), runStory awaits ui.say then calls gen.next(result). Implementation:

export async function runStory(genFn, ctx) {
 const gen = genFn(ctx);
 let next = gen.next();
 while (!next.done) {
   const cmd = next.value;
   let result = await exec(cmd, ctx);
   next = gen.next(result);
 }
}

Commands:
- {t:'say', who, text, portrait}
- {t:'choice', options:[{text,value,req,note,hide}]}
- {t:'flag', key, value}
- {t:'give', item, n}
- {t:'gold', n}
- {t:'join', id}
- {t:'battle', ...} returns result
- {t:'shop', shopId}
- {t:'heal'}
- {t:'travel', zone, x, y}
- {t:'toast', text, icon}
- {t:'cinematic', lines, opts}
- {t:'modal', ...}
- {t:'ending', data}
- {t:'wait', ms}
- {t:'quest', id, status}
- {t:'xp', n}
- {t:'sp', n}
- {t:'startQuest', id}, etc
- {t:'music', scene}
- {t:'sfx', name}
- {t:'save'}
- {t:'if'}? Generators can branch naturally.

On battle defeat: story engine handles: heal, lose gold already battle did, respawn to last crystal via hooks.respawn or world.enterZone, set a ctx flag and abort story. Requirement from summary: "on story battle defeat restore + travel to last crystal and abort." So exec battle:
const res = await startBattle(...)
if (res?.defeat) { toast('...'); await fade; hooks.respawn?.(); throw new StoryAbort? } But runStory must abort gracefully. Could set ctx.aborted=true and generator command loop stops. exec returns maybe {defeat:true}; runStory checks and returns. We can have runStory return when result?.abort. Define a custom sentinel: exec returns {__abort:true}. runStory sees and breaks.

Careful battle's startBattle only restores party on defeat but doesn't travel. hooks.respawn is main/world respawnPlayer which enterZone. world.js exports respawnPlayer. Story imports hooks? Or ctx.world has enterZone? ctx.world is imported world object (not module). Better import { hooks } from './hooks.js' and call hooks.respawn?.(). main wires hooks.respawn = respawnPlayer. Or use dynamic import of world? Circular import if story imports world. Use hooks to avoid cycle.

Also story calls hooks.openShop, hooks.travel? We can import hooks and call `hooks.openShop?.(shopId)`. That's manageable. For travel during story: hooks.travel?.(zone,x,y). main travel should support paused context? Need careful. Story run with world.paused true. hooks.travel from main maybe calls enterZone. We'll design main's travel wrapper to work.

For shop: `openShop` uses ui-shop and pauses. Story yields shop; runStory calls await hooks.openShop(shopId) where openShop returns Promise resolving when closed. We'll design.

Need dialogue IDs list:
hearthfall: intro, elder, smith, innkeeper, herbalist, child, seer, guard.
emberfield: intro, wren, dax, pilgrim, merchant, emberfield_crossroads.
greenwood: intro, seris, lyra, fen, quill, thea, bramble, woodchild, grove_confrontation, grove_heart_hint, grove_heart (boss).

citadel: intro, citadel_hall, final_boss.

Need story mechanics:
- Prologue: Hearthfall intro triggers automatically at start. Player can move after. Story state. On first entry, intro should probably be narration and direct to Maro. Then elder story: festival, crown, attack? Prologue sets prologueDone, gives kael, maybe first battle with ashling to teach. Should be immediately playable. On prologueDone, objective points to Emberfield. Kael joins. Maybe elder gives 3 tonics, 60 gold, hearthsigil. Also intro should not auto-run every zone? `state.flags['intro_'+id]` world handles.

- Keys: each zone boss gives key:
  - Greenwood: grove_heart -> Thornwarden; after victory, choose? thorn key. Grove choice earlier between Seris (Wardens) and Lyra (Freewood) influences boss framing and companion. Need `groveChoice` flag = 'warden' or 'freewood'. grove_confrontation at center before boss triggers when entering ring. Seris and Lyra both at edges. The trigger cond !groveChoice. Choice with them: side with Warden or Freewood. Companion joins. Then grove_heart_hint after choice. The altar's grove_heart story: boss fight. On victory set keyThorn, add emberkey_thorn, set greenwoodBossDefeated, act progress. Perhaps after boss, branch epilogue based on choice.
  - Mire: sable meet; witch boss at altar. Spare choice after fight: `sparedWitch`; if spared, sable joins (party has room? hero+kael+lyra/seris = 3, so room yes), witch shop appears. moonpetal side quest with witch. Key tide.
  - Peaks: Malrec proposes alliance / take crown; choices peaksChoice 'order' or 'refuse' maybe 'claim'. Boss knightCommander Vurn. Then prisoner choice maybe. Key cinder.
  - Citadel: needs keys, triggers hall story, final boss Vaelor; final choice "claim crown", "shatter crown", "give crown to ..." Endings multiple.
  - Act progression: state.act maybe 1 after prologue, 2 after keys? mainObjective uses act>=3. Set act 2 after prologue, act 3 after 3 keys or citadel entry.

- Final boss: Vaelor phases: first vaelor, then maybe vaelorUnbound if choice? To keep manageable, final_boss: battle vaelor, then ending choice; perhaps if "claim crown" -> battle vaelorUnbound then ending? That may be too hard but cool. Could do final battle only, choice after. Endings data variations.

- NG+: main handles creation with legacy; story should show `ngPlus` epilogue in citadel intro / ending. `state.ngPlus` incremented on continue. Ending screen button "Begin the Continuation" sets state.ngPlus++ and returns to creation with legacy=true; main must preserve previous completion metadata. Need design.

Endings:
- dawnforge (shatter crown, free flame)
- ashcrown (claim crown)
- wardenkeep (bind crown to wardens) if groveChoice warden / peaksChoice order?
- freewood (give to Freewood)
- sacrifice (Vaelor redeemed?)
Need choice options limited but meaningful. `buildEndingData(choice)` returns {id,title,kicker,body,choices,legacy}. ENDINGS object.

Use flags: groveChoice, sparedWitch, peaksChoice, sable joined, etc.

2. Choice: "Fight him" / "Hear him out" (both lead to fight).

`runStory`:
```
export async function runStory(story, ctx={}) {
  let gen = typeof story === 'function' ? story(ctx) : story;
  if (!gen || typeof gen.next !== 'function') return;
  let res = gen.next();
  while (!res.done) {
    const out = await exec(res.value, ctx);
    if (out && out.__abort) return {aborted:true};
    res = gen.next(out);
  }
  return res.value;
}
```

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D turn-based JRPG for phone/tablet with character creation, job classes, skill trees, open-world exploration, and choices-matter branching storylines with continuation arcs.
- Work is in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround` (static HTML/JS project, uncommitted).

## Requirements
- 2D game playable on phone/tablet; responsive touch controls; usable in landscape and portrait.
- Turn-based JRPG combat, character creation, job classes, skill trees, open world, choices-matter story with continuation arcs.
- No clarifying questions; note assumptions briefly at finish.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for own checks; viewport ≤1280px; read only latest screenshot.
- Must be a complete, playable build now.
- Static `index.html` at repo root served by runtime.

## Decisions
- Vanilla ES modules + canvas rendering + DOM UI; no build step, no external art/audio assets.
- Title: **Emberwake — The Ashen Crown**.
- 6 classes: `vanguard`, `emberweaver`, `shadowblade`, `warden`, `stormcaller`, `ronin`; each with a 10-node skill tree.
- 3 origins: `hearthbound`, `scholar`, `outcast`; 6 appearance palettes; 3 bonus stat points.
- 6 zones: `hearthfall`, `emberfield`, `greenwood`, `mire`, `peaks`, `citadel`.
- Party max 4: hero + Kael (always after prologue) + Lyra or Seris (Greenwood choice) + optional Sable (spare Mire witch).
- Act structure: prologue → collect 3 Emberkeys in any order → Hollow Citadel → Vaelor → branching endings + NG+ continuation.
- Procedural WebAudio music/SFX; all art drawn procedurally on canvas.
- Save to `localStorage` (`emberwake.chronicle.v1`, autosave `emberwake.autosave.v1`).
- Story command protocol implemented in `js/story.js` (`say`, `choice`, `flag`, `give`, `battle`, `shop`, `heal`, `travel`, `cinematic`, `modal`, `ending`, etc.); story battles abort + respawn on defeat.
- Final ending IDs: `shatter`, `claim`, `warden`, `freewood`, `mercy`; `claim` triggers an extra `vaelorUnbound` battle first.
- NG+ stores `state.ngPlus`, `state.legacy`, `state.legacyEnding`, `state.legacyName`, `state.legacyClass`.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` app shell with title, creation, HUD, dialogue, menu, shop, battle UI, cinematic, ending, modal layers.
- `css/style.css` responsive dark ember/teal styling including touch joystick, menus, battle layout, ending, safe areas.
- Data: `js/data/classes.js`, `items.js`, `enemies.js`, `zones.js`.
- `js/state.js`: progression, stats, XP/leveling, skills, party, inventory, quests, saves; added legacy/NG+ carry fields.
- Engine modules: `audio.js`, `art.js`, `world-render.js`, `title-render.js`, `battle-render.js`, `ui-core.js`, `ui-create.js`, `ui-battle.js`, `ui-menu.js`, `ui-shop.js`.
- `js/world.js`: exploration, collision/pathfinding, interactions, chests/crystals/braziers/sparkles/signs/altars, portals, triggers, random encounters, story dispatch.
- `js/battle.js`: full turn queue, skills/items/guard/flee, statuses, enemy AI, boss enrage, rewards/level-ups, defeat respawn result.
- `js/story.js`: all required `STORIES` IDs, prologue, side quests, Grove/Mire/Peaks choices, bosses, Citadel finale, five endings, dynamic ending data.
- `js/main.js`: boot, hooks, title/continue/help/sound/fullscreen, scene loop, DPR resize, world/battle/ending rendering, NG+ path.
- All JS files pass `node --check`.
- Server running at `http://localhost:3002` in tmux session `emberwake`; HTTP 200.
- Playwright Chromium installed; title, creation steps, world entry, and cinematic intro verified with JPEG screenshots.
- Console currently shows 0 errors/0 warnings.

### Active
- End-to-end gameplay test after prologue cinematic: Elder dialogue, prologue battle, menus/shop, saves, zone transitions, bosses, endings.
- Responsive/mobile viewport verification still pending.
- Git commit/push still pending.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Advance the intro cinematic using a real mouse click at screen center (`playwright-cli run-code` worked); `playwright-cli click "#cine-skip"` did not reliably advance.
2. Walk to Elder Maro (`18,8`), trigger prologue dialogue/battle, verify Kael joins, HUD updates, save, and objective changes.
3. Test menu tabs, skills, satchel/equip, shop buy/sell, crystal rest/save, random encounter, defeat respawn.
4. Exercise all zones/bosses/story choices and at least one ending + NG+ continuation.
5. Capture fresh JPEG screenshots for desktop and phone/tablet viewports; fix visual/runtime issues.
6. Commit and push when satisfied.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/story.js`: all narrative, quests, choices, bosses, endings.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: boot, hooks, canvas loop, title/ending handling, NG+.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/engine/ui-shop.js`: shop tabs/buy/sell/talk, `openShop`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`: exploration loop and story/battle integration; exports `enterZone`, `respawnPlayer`, `setPaused`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/battle.js`: battle engine and `startBattle`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/state.js`: central state, save/load, party, NG+ legacy fields.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/data/zones.js`: maps, NPCs, chests, triggers, portals, bosses.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/engine/ui-core.js`: dialogue, choice, cinematic, modal, HUD helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/engine/ui-menu.js`: menu tabs, skill tree, map, system/help.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/engine/ui-battle.js`: battle DOM/action targeting/results.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: required IDs used by all UI modules.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: responsive layout and all visual styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: latest JPEG verification captures.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/hooks.js`: hook registry wired by `main.js`.

- Server: `tmux new-session -d -s emberwake "RUNTIME_DIR=$RUNTIME_DIR PORT=3002 bash start.sh"`; logs at `/tmp/opencode/emberwake-server.log`.
- Playwright browser path: `/home/runner/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome`; was installed via `playwright-cli install-browser chromium`.
- Open page: `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`; screenshot: `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/latest.jpg`.

- Prologue battle enemies: 2 × `ashling` level 1; boss levels set to Thornwarden 5, Mire Witch 7, Vurn 9, Vaelor 12, Unbound Flame 12.
- `world.runDialogue` pauses world; story battle defeat calls `fade`, `hooks.respawn()`, `restoreParty(true)`, then aborts remaining story.
- `state.createHero` preserves prior `ngPlus`/`legacy` values and legacy metadata; title “New Chronicle” clears them.
- Continue detects `state.ending` and re-renders the saved epilogue.
- Working tree is uncommitted; no commit/push yet.
